subject: Aurelia: finalizing SLA bundle pricing and coverage
messages:
From: Marcus Lee <m.lee@aureliahealth.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Final SLA ask — uptime / credits / response lanes

Chloe —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We're close on budget but need to lock SLA economics before procurement will move forward. High-level asks from Aurelia: 
- Target uptime: aim for 99.95% (we run mission-critical routing)
- P1 response: 1 hour to acknowledge, 4 hour remediation target (we'll accept playbook-driven remediation)
- Regional failover included (multi-region) — we need a clear escalation playbook and runbook handoff
- Credits: we want a predictable credit matrix tied to downtime minutes and a monthly cap

Two commercial constraints on our side: a 12-month procurement horizon with a fixed budget line, and a request to minimize any one-time onboarding fees. If you can share a simple tiered pricing grid and what a 12-month commit discount looks like, I can push this to procurement.

Attaching our requirements doc for context (ops@aureliahealth.com is on the thread).

Cheers,
Marcus
Head of SRE, Aurelia Health

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lee <m.lee@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Final SLA ask — uptime / credits / response lanes

Marcus — thanks for the clear list, and glad the demo landed. Looping in Jonas (pricing) and Kimberly (security/compliance) so we can answer the regional and onboarding questions. Below is a concise options breakdown — I also attached a more detailed pricing grid.

Option A — Standard Response
- Uptime: 99.90%
- P1 acknowledge: 1 hour; target remediation: 8 hours
- Regional failover: available as add-on (per-region multiplier)
- Credits: per-event credit up to 10% monthly cap
- One-time onboarding: $5k
- Typical use case: non-production or batch-critical applications

Option B — Premium (recommended for Aurelia)
- Uptime: 99.95%
- P1 acknowledge: 1 hour; target remediation: 4 hours (playbook-driven)
- Regional failover: included for primary+1 region
- Credits: graded credit matrix (minutes-based) with a 5% monthly cap
- One-time onboarding: $1.5k (reduced for annual commit)
- 12-month commit discount: 15% off base monthly fee; 24-month: 22%

Notes and ask: 
- We can waive the onboarding fee if you agree to a 12-month prepay or a minimum monthly commit (e.g., $XXk/month).
- For the regional failover you asked about, Kimberly will confirm compliance controls for cross-region failover (data residency / logging).
- I'll need a confirmed committed TCV or target monthly spend so Jonas can produce a final quote and a DocuSign link.

I've attached SLA_pricing_grid_v3.xlsx with the math and credit tables. Please review and tell us which option you prefer and whether procurement will accept a 12-month commit (prepay vs monthly invoicing).

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call if that helps tighten the terms.

Best,
Chloe Martin

Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Final SLA ask — uptime / credits / response lanes

Chloe / team —

Appreciate the clear options. A few follow-ups from procurement and SRE: 
- Onboarding fee: procurement will push back on any upfront professional fee unless it can be demonstrated as optional. Can you remove the onboarding line and bake any one-time work into the first-month invoice or credits?
- Discount: 15% for 12 months is good, but we were hoping to see 20% for a firm 12-month commit (annual billing) given our ARR profile. Any flexibility there?
- Multiregion: the primary+1 include needs to explicitly cover failover RTO for cross-region cold start. Can you confirm operational steps and a named SLA contact in the escalation ladder?

Quoted for context: 
> "We can waive the onboarding fee if you agree to a 12-month prepay or a minimum monthly commit (prepay vs monthly invoicing)."

If you can send a final quote with the two variants (12m @ 15% and 12m @ 20% with onboarding baked in) that would help procurement decide quickly. If you require, we'll schedule a short call next week with our procurement lead and SRE.

Thanks,
Marcus

Marcus — Chloe —

Short answer: we can meet the 99.95% premium terms and support the 1hr P1 acknowledge / 4hr remediation target with the following commercial tweaks to address procurement asks: 
- Offer 12-month annual billing at 20% discount (requires signed DocuSign agreement and annual invoice).
- Onboarding: we will waive the standalone onboarding fee and roll the estimated one-time setup (~$1.5k) into month 1 as a line-item credit, effectively zeroing the upfront ask if you sign the 12-month annual invoice.
- Regional failover: we include primary+1 as stated; operationally we'll provide a named escalation contact (Tier 2 SRE) and a cold-start runbook with a 30-min warm-start checklist. This will be part of the runbook handoff in the onboarding folder.
- Credits: we'll adopt the Premium graded matrix (5% monthly cap). For very high-impact customers we can increase the cap with a reserve retainer — happy to discuss if Aurelia needs that.

Next steps: 
1) Chloe — will you confirm acceptance of the 20% annual billing option?
2) Marcus — if accepted, I'll generate the final quote and DocuSign. Expect the DocuSign link to include the annual invoice and a single SOW addendum for onboarding runbook delivery.
